item.text: {"groups":[{"member_ids":["459a93f0538f947ff3c8","bbe1a218d5b167101aba"],"operation":"Dump a value loaded by json_loadb through do_dump.","condition":"Dump traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.","capability":"do_dump returns failure at the depth limit.","consequence":"A depth-limit rejection cannot be exercised if json_loadb does not admit a value that reaches it.","equivalence_reason":"Both candidates concern the same do_dump depth guard, its parser-dependent trigger, and its failure result."},{"member_ids":["2d961f56c0c65878aac3","5fa983009411d6b995ac"],"operation":"Call json_dumps for string output.","condition":"The input requests nonzero indentation through JSON_MAX_INDENT.","capability":"json_dumps passes indentation flags to dump_indent to produce indented output.","consequence":"Clearing JSON_MAX_INDENT prevents that string-output behavior from being exercised.","equivalence_reason":"Both candidates describe the same flag mask, formatting capability, and effect on json_dumps."},{"member_ids":["5822aab2a17e20ff00a6"],"operation":"Dump a loaded value through json_dump_callback.","condition":"The callback rejects output.","capability":"do_dump propagates callback failure.","consequence":"A callback that always returns zero cannot exercise the rejection path.","equivalence_reason":"This callback-failure path has a different trigger and consequence from the depth and indentation hypotheses."}]}
